correctness.rationale: An indexed embedding maps position i to the window [i,i+2]. Candidate sets for distinct i are disjoint: intersecting windows have source distance at most two and the matching symbol would have to be equal. A host with an embedding has all m sets nonempty and at most two surplus positions. Consequently a host with at least three embeddings has one size-three set or two size-two sets; every host position is then in a candidate set. A size-three set occupies the whole three-site window; any other singleton must occur on the correct side of the window (some embedding exists and no singleton is inside it). This is exactly tripling one occurrence of a source letter, even if that letter recurs elsewhere. Two size-two windows at distance at least two cannot invert their picks because their ranges meet at most in a single position and the sets are disjoint. Compatibility with fixed singleton neighbors therefore factors, yielding four embeddings exactly when both duplicated positions have both choices available, forcing adjacent copies by exhaustion of host positions. At distance one the four positions fill one block starting with a and ending with b; aabb has four indexed choices and abab has three. The locations in each constructed host are uniquely retrievable from its surplus-candidate indices, so none of these host families overcounts. This includes m=1, where only tripling occurs, and m=2, where distance two is vacuous. Greedy scanning counts the ordinary insertion sphere S; double-counting pairs (host, embedding) gives Z=q^2*binom(m+2,2). Thus Z-S=N2+2N3+3N4 proves the remaining histogram, including zeros, by algebra. Uniform input and uniformly chosen masks give posterior weight e/Z. The entropy correction numerator is 2q*m^2+O_q(m) and denominator (q^2/2)*m^2+O_q(m), so the limit correction is 4/q with the stated uniformity. Sequentially choosing distinct next letters gives q(q-1)(q-2)^(m-2) targets for m>=2 and forces period-three continuation for q=3. No global entropy extremum follows or is claimed.
correctness.reproduction: Independent exhaustive finite check, without running the source checker: for each q=3,4,5 use all host words for target lengths 1 through 6,5,4 respectively. For every such x loop over all m retained-position combinations, obtain y by reading those positions, and accumulate one unit in the table indexed by (y,x) when y is locally distinct (also retain the two specified boundary targets in the ternary length-three case). Derive N0 by subtracting the number of observed compatible hosts from q^(m+2); compare every histogram and the two high-multiplicity host sets to the formulas. This enumerates 51,152 hosts and 930,789 masks and checks 482 locally distinct targets. Ternary 010 had counts by r=0,1,2,3,4 of (192,23,21,3,4); 001 had (192,31,8,9,1) and two multiplicity-six hosts. All matched. The frozen verifier and output were inspected as evidence; its published 484,024 counts distinct full-host/target evaluations in its grid, not literal function calls, since its filter recomputes the positive counts. None of the finite checks is used as an unbounded proof.

evidence: Bruda gives an earlier exact formula that directly covers N1: with target length and run count both m, his Appendix A.2 gives N1=[z^2](1-(q-1)z)^(-2)(1-(q-2)z)^(-(m-1)). Multiplying the first three coefficients gives the same row. Section 4.1 discusses a broader sufficiently-long-host polynomial-exponential shape for general multiplicity and mentions an in-preparation proof, not the short-host evaluated coefficients.

value.rationale: The fixed received-word embedding spectrum is the actual posterior uncertainty in the exact-two-deletion channel. A locally distinct target is a natural nonbinary way to suppress short repeats while still allowing repeated symbols later. The exact support and high-multiplicity classes quantify what ambiguity remains, including the adjacent alternating insertion and a posterior entropy deficit of 4/q bits in the long-target limit. This is more than recalculating the prior sphere size or the prior single-embedding count and does not assert entropy maximization.
